source.hook_line: The One who made every ocean gasped two words on a cross: I thirst.
source.spoken_script: The One who made every ocean gasped two words on a cross: I thirst. Psalm twenty-two. David wrote it in the first person, but he was picturing someone else's death. Watch the body give out: "My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue cleaveth to my jaws; and thou hast brought me into the dust of death." Dried clay; a tongue stuck fast; a man sinking into the dust of death. Then John records the dying Jesus' cry: "I thirst." Psalm twenty-two does not foretell that cry — it paints the thirst behind it, a thousand years before He felt it. The One who offers the world living water hung there dry, in your place. Bring Him your thirst — and drink. That water is Himself.

The One who made every ocean gasped two words on a cross (John 19:28): I thirst.

A thousand years earlier, Psalm 22 painted the thirst behind that cry. David wrote in the first person, but he was picturing someone else's death: "My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue cleaveth to my jaws; and thou hast brought me into the dust of death."

Dried clay. A tongue stuck fast. A man sinking into the dust of death.

Then John records it: "After this, Jesus knowing that all things were now accomplished, that the scripture might be fulfilled, saith, I thirst" (John 19:28, KJV).

The One who offers the world living water hung there dry, in your place.

Bring him your thirst, and drink. That water is himself.

platforms.label: YouTube (Long-form 16:9)
platforms.title: I Thirst: The Cry Psalm 22 Painted a Thousand Years Early
platforms.description:
Of the seven sayings from the cross (John 19:28), the shortest is two words: I thirst.

It sounds almost small beside the others. It is not. A thousand years before Golgotha, Psalm 22 painted the dying body behind that cry: "My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue cleaveth to my jaws; and thou hast brought me into the dust of death." Dried clay. A tongue stuck fast. The dust of death.

And then John's eyewitness line: "After this, Jesus knowing that all things were now accomplished, that the scripture might be fulfilled, saith, I thirst" (John 19:28, KJV).

Notice what John notices: Jesus speaks the cry KNOWING all things were now accomplished. Even his thirst walks inside the Scriptures.

And the deepest turn: this is the same voice that stood up at a feast and offered living water to anyone who would come. The Giver of living water hung there dry, in your place, so that your thirst could be answered forever.

In this piece: the potsherd line in David's psalm, John's fulfilment note, and the exchange inside two small words.

Bring him your thirst, and drink. That water is himself.
